monitoring.note: Written by hand from the Drivechain Talk Telegram group, the betanet branch of ecash-com/bitcoin and BitWindow's own network catalog. There is no watcher job on this page and no official eCash document behind it.

headline: The betanet forks Bitcoin at block 967,680 — and nothing carries over.
message: Stage two of three. Betanet is a fresh chain that forks away from Bitcoin at block 967,680 — the first block of Bitcoin's 480th difficulty period, expected during Saturday 19 September 2026. It issues practice coins (pECX) again: the permanent 1:1 ECX credit for Bitcoin holders still only happens at mainnet, around BTC block 973,728. What changes for anyone who was on the Alphanet is that the Alphanet ends here: those coins are not on the betanet, so the burning, selling or wrapping of alpha pECX has to be finished before the fork block lands.

fork.height_note: First block of Bitcoin's 480th difficulty period — 2016 × 480, and consensus.EcashHeight = 967680 in src/kernel/chainparams.cpp on the betanet branch ("Retarget boundary, 2016 * 480"). All three eCash stages sit on a difficulty boundary: alpha at 963,648 (478), beta at 967,680 (480), mainnet at 973,728 (483).
fork.eta: Saturday 19 September 2026, most likely around 08:00 UTC
fork.eta_detail: The block-height clock is the real one, not the calendar. At 18 September 07:00 UTC Bitcoin stood at 967,524 — 156 blocks, or 26 hours at Bitcoin's current average of 578 s, which puts the fork at about 08:00 UTC on the 19th (up to about 09:00 if blocks slow back to the 600 s target). That matches ecpool.tech's own estimate of ~08:00 UTC; epool.cash's ~13:40 UTC (written on 17 September) is the later end of the same window. Recompute it yourself: today's Bitcoin height, subtracted from 967,680, times ten to twelve minutes.
fork.mainnet: ECX mainnet at BTC block 973,728 — on or around 31 October 2026 (the Bitcoin whitepaper's 18th birthday), or as early as 29 October at the current block pace. That is where the permanent 1:1 ECX balance is credited to every Bitcoin address; 6,204 blocks away at the same reading.

facts.v: pECX again — practice coins, not the real thing
facts.note: Permanent ECX is created only at mainnet. Alpha and beta both mint practice coins, and alpha's are discarded at this fork.

New in betanet: the block at the fork height must carry that exact target, and the node rejects any other (bad-diffbits-ecash-da). That is about 7 PH/s of SHA-256 to find one block every ten minutes — trivial next to Bitcoin, then normal 2,016-block retargeting resumes.

facts.v: Own network magic 0xeca5b104, P2P port 8533, RPC 8532
facts.note: Bitcoin's ledger and Bitcoin's genesis block, with eCash's own magic and ports, so the two nodes cannot cross-connect. Same addresses and same seed phrase as Bitcoin: the same key controls the coins on both chains.

facts.v: Opt-in, by a magic nLockTime of 499,999,999
facts.note: A transaction carrying that nLockTime is treated as final on eCash but is still valid on Bitcoin, so it will not be replayed backwards. The fork does not split coins for you.

The node refuses getblocktemplate from anyone who does not acknowledge the bip300301 rule, and marks its templates !bip300301 — a plain L1 template has no sidechain commitments and would orphan sidechain activity.

facts.v: Ends at this fork — abandoned, not migrated
facts.note: Alpha and beta are separate ledgers that each fork from a later Bitcoin block height. Nothing you mined, named or deposited on the alphanet exists on the betanet.

facts.v: Must be burned, sold or wrapped before the fork
facts.note: The burn credits 1/100 of what you burn as mainnet ECX (ceil(burn/100), minimum strictly above 1,000). After the alphanet stops, coins left there are not redeemable.

facts.v: Reported at twice the alpha credit — 20 ECX per 1,000 burned
facts.note: An L2L developer in the group put the same 1,013.4 pECX burn at 10.134 ECX on alpha and "20.268 extra for the betanet-burn". The wallet implementation only ships the alphanet rate (ceil(burn/100)), so the beta rate is a statement, not code I could read.

facts.v: None have committed to alpha or beta
facts.note: The stated point of the beta stage is to put the chain in front of exchanges, wallet providers, miners and custodians. Whether any of them credit beta pECX (or, later, mainnet ECX) is each venue's decision, and no announcement exists yet.

sections.title: What actually happens at the fork

items.title: The last Bitcoin block before 967,680 mines as normal.
items.detail: Bitcoin is untouched throughout. Nothing about BTC, its addresses or its balances changes.

items.title: At 967,680, betanet starts its own chain from Bitcoin's ledger.
items.detail: It copies the state of Bitcoin's ledger at that height, exactly as the alphanet did at 963,648 — same addresses, same keys, same seed phrase. What you can actually spend on the betanet is what you mine or buy there. Practice coins are credited into real ECX at mainnet only through the burn, and the 1:1 credit for Bitcoin holders arrives at mainnet and nowhere before it.

items.title: The first betanet block is pinned at difficulty 1e9.
items.detail: Unlike alpha, which started without a fixed target, the betanet enforces bits 0x19044b7e on the block at the fork height. Miners can plan for it — and anyone with rented hashrate should, because at 1e9 the first hours are far cheaper than Bitcoin.

items.title: Everyone's alpha balances stay on the abandoned alpha chain.
items.detail: "Alpha, beta, mainnet all fork from a later BTC block height, they don't continue from themselves." pECX on the alphanet is not pECX on the betanet, and bitnames, sidechain assets and wrapped positions on alpha have to be re-created if they are supported at all.

items.title: Node operators move to the beta branch; the wallet reuses the alpha blocks.
items.detail: BitWindow notifies you that you can switch, and offers to reuse the alphanet blocks you already downloaded instead of re-syncing — in the GUI and on the CLI. Only the header chain beyond the fork is new. There is no assumeutxo snapshot published for the betanet yet; the reuse path exists because of that.

items.title: The burning window for the alpha move ends with the fork.
items.detail: Burn before you switch networks. A burn submitted after the last alpha block stops being mined never gets past the mempool: "So what happens if you submit the coins for burning, but no block gets mined because everyone moves on to the beta net?"

sections.title: If you are holding alpha pECX
paragraphs: The alphanet is retired at the fork. Three routes were published by the community before the deadline, and only the first one is L2L's own mechanism.

items.title: Burn them in BitWindow, before the fork block.
items.detail: Send more than 1,000 pECX to the eater address with the wallet's own first address in an OP_RETURN. The credit is 1/100 rounded up — 1,013.4 pECX becomes 10.134 ECX at mainnet. The card only exists on Alphanet, and it needs a software wallet that can sign.

items.title: Sell them.
items.detail: There is a thin market, and it prices pECX as practice coins. Nothing about that market is official.

items.title: Wrap them into a Solana token.
items.detail: A community member offered to peg alpha pECX 1:1 into a Solana token that can be traded in the six weeks before mainnet, with a beta token to follow. This is a third party taking custody, not a protocol feature.

sections.title: If you are mining
paragraphs: The pools are the reason to plan ahead: beta starts at 1e9 difficulty, so early blocks are cheap enough that rented hashrate will chase them — the alpha comparison was a few hundred dollars of rented hash for about 2,000 pECX, and beta pays double on the burn. The pools that switched on at the first instant were taking registrations the day before.

items.title: ecpool.tech — mining.ecpool.tech:3334
items.detail: The pool formerly named ecashpool.tech. "Same pool, new name. We are ready for the ECX betanet." It announced that it is already mining, with the engine switching to the betanet at the hardfork.

items.title: epool.cash — mine.epool.cash:3334 (rentals: :3335)
items.detail: Mining pool built on DATUM; the operator automated the switch so the pool is on betanet from the first block. Their own landing page carries the current estimate and the connect guide.

items.title: pool.beta.bip300.xyz — stratum+tcp://pool.beta.bip300.xyz:3334
items.detail: The pool BitWindow's own network catalog lists for the betanet, with 3335 for rented/aggregated hashrate and 3336 for NiceHash. It pays in the block's own coinbase (pplns-coinbase) and holds no balance for you.

items.title: Alphanet pools are winding down
items.detail: The alphanet's own catalog entry points at pool.alpha.avonpool.xyz:3334. Alpha mining kept running until the fork, but the coins stop counting at it.

sections.title: If you run a node or BitWindow

items.title: Software
items.detail: The betanet branch of ecash-com/bitcoin has existed since the morning of 16 September (ecash-com/bitcoin @ betanet, plus betanet-bridge for the replay feed). releases.drivechain.info still carries alphanet and forknet binaries only — check there for the beta node and enforcer zips rather than trusting a mirror.

items.title: What the betanet changes in the code
items.detail: Difficulty pin at the fork height; own magic and ports; eCash seed nodes replacing Bitcoin's; OP_DRIVECHAIN made standard; the getblocktemplate rule that forces mining through the enforcer; and a tagged signet magic so an eCash signet cannot collide with Bitcoin's.

items.title: Peers and services
items.detail: DNS seeds: seed.beta.ecash.ninja, seed.beta.bip300.xyz, seed.beta.ecash.drivecha.in, seed.beta.ecash.zuexeuz.net. Esplora at esplora.beta.ecash.ninja, Fulcrum at ssl://explorer.beta.ecash.ninja:50002, explorer at explorer.beta.ecash.ninja. BitWindow's betanet entry was updated on 17 September to carry the Esplora URL so light-mode users see balances.

items.title: The alphanet snapshot trap
items.detail: The alphanet's bundled assumeutxo snapshot was the fork block itself, so an enforcer built from it stalled at 963,647 waiting for a base block that assumeutxo never downloads. If you hit that on alpha, the workaround is a snapshot whose base sits below the fork height — and it is the reason the betanet has no snapshot of its own to offer yet.

items.title: The replay problem that beta inherits
items.detail: On alpha, the ECX chain mined Bitcoin's shared mempool at activation, so every transaction that users fee-bumped on Bitcoin afterwards became a permanent split; the replay rate fell from 96% to about 9%. A community fix (a block-driven BTC-to-ECX feed that only injects BTC-confirmed transactions) exists as a branch and has to be rebased onto the beta branch to run at this fork.

warnings: There is still no official specification. drivechain.info/dev.txt is unchanged since 19 February 2026 and does not mention the betanet, ecash.com carries no beta parameters, and the numbers on this page come from the project's Telegram group, the code, and the network catalog BitWindow ships with.
Beta pECX is not money. It is a practice coin on a chain that will be abandoned in favour of mainnet in the same way alpha is being abandoned now.
Holding BTC gets you nothing at this fork. The 1:1 ECX credit for Bitcoin holders happens at mainnet, block ~973,728, against the keys that control your BTC then.
Burn before the fork, not after. Exactly 1,000 pECX is not enough (the threshold is exclusive) and there is no topping up. Burned coins are unrecoverable by design.

Do not follow fork, claim, swap or migration guides from random websites, videos, chats or DMs. Nobody legitimate needs your seed phrase or private key, and nobody can hand you beta ECX for a payment.
Third-party tokens, pools, wrappers and swap sites are not part of the protocol and are not endorsed here. Check who holds the keys before you trust a peg.
